title: Trains to Clacton
lead: These are the trains I would look at for the Clacton Air Show. Greater Anglia runs a direct train from London Liverpool Street to Clacton-on-Sea every hour, and you can get there from its other main stations too, with a change at Colchester or Shenfield. Pick your station, a day and a time below and the map shows every station on the way.
ysIntro: This is the station I would get off at for the Clacton Air Show. The details below follow the train you pick further down the page.
walkLine: From the station it’s about 10 to 15 minutes on foot. Head down through the town centre to the seafront, then turn right for the West Greensward.
walkBack: Allow about 15 minutes to walk back up to the station from the West Greensward, and a bit more when the crowds leave.
legs: Out past Bethnal Green and through Stratford. You run alongside the Elizabeth line most of the way to Shenfield, so it’s one of the busiest bits of railway in the country.
This is where it opens out into the Essex countryside. Some trains stop at Ingatestone on the way, so check your train in the station list.
Past the new Beaulieu Park station and on through Witham. A few trains also call at Hatfield Peverel, Kelvedon and Marks Tey.
After Colchester the train leaves the main line, calls at Hythe and follows the River Colne down to Wivenhoe. Some trains stop at Alresford, Great Bentley and Weeley too.
Thorpe-le-Soken is where the line to Walton-on-the-Naze goes its own way. From here it’s the last few minutes down to Clacton, the end of the line.
tip: Trains are very busy straight after the flying, as everyone heads for the station at once. I would either leave a little early, or stay in town for something to eat and catch a later train.
On the Thursday there’s the twilight display. In the current timetable the last direct train to London leaves Clacton at 22:05, so I would check this before the twilight display starts.
Greater Anglia usually adds extra trains on airshow days, and the summer 2027 times come out nearer the show, so please check before you travel.
alt: When I last checked, an off-peak day return from London was £53.90, or £44.10 super off-peak on trains from about midday.
If you’re going as a family, a Family and Friends Railcard takes a third off adult fares and 60% off children’s fares. It may well pay for itself on this one trip.
note: Due to how complicated the rail network is, this page only shows train services run by Greater Anglia. Times are from the National Rail timetable for Thursday 5 and Friday 6 November 2026, checked on 30 October 2026. Times for summer 2027 usually come out in the spring, so please check with Greater Anglia before you travel. The line is drawn along the railway, so treat it as a guide.
